bug_semantics: The default-registered strip_html filter applied one global regular expression containing unbounded lazy script, style, comment, and generic-tag alternatives directly to attacker-controlled template data. On many opener tokens without a matching closer, V8 retries an alternative at each '<' and scans the remaining suffix looking for the absent terminator, producing quadratic work on the single Node.js event-loop thread. memoryLimit did not bound that CPU work because it charged only the input string length before String.replace ran.
flaw_origin: Commit 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 replaced the prior simple tag regex in filters.js with the Ruby-Liquid-compatible /<script.*?<\/script>|<!--.*?-->|<style.*?<\/style>|<.*?>/g expression. That functional-parity change first introduced the unbounded lazy alternatives and therefore the vulnerable repeated-suffix search; later moves and expansions preserved or broadened the same mechanism rather than originating it.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object identifies human author Paul Robert Lloyd <me+git@paulrobertlloyd.com> and human committer Jun Yang <harttle@harttle.com>; its message is only 'Ensure strip_html filter uses same regex as Ruby Liquid' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/security/advisories/GHSA-r7g9-xpmj-5fcq identifies src/filters/html.ts strip_html, explains the O(N^2) failed-closer search for '<script'.repeat(N), and references fix 3616a744b9abeb425c217b340a2397d46176afb8. `git log -L 48,48:src/filters/html.ts 3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed` traced the regex through 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045, e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2, 42d25902e855d3c06d5ead071bf55604f495c205, file moves/renames, and ultimately the substantive introduction at 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887. `git show 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887` shows the one-line replacement from /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g to the four lazy alternatives plus matching behavior tests. Direct parent-tree verification with `git grep -n "'strip_html'" f668a5cc4188c4b2ad82c0dbcdd31e6e5bb95aae -- filters.js` returned only the old simple regex, proving the flawed mechanism absent from the immediate parent. Boundary comparison showed v3.1.2 contains the old regex while v3.1.3 contains the introduced lazy-alternative regex; `git tag --contains 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 --sort=version:refname` begins at v3.1.3. At the patch boundary, v10.25.7 still contains the vulnerable regex, v10.26.0 contains the new indexOf/Map single-pass scanner, and `git tag --contains 3616a744b9abeb425c217b340a2397d46176afb8 --sort=version:refname` begins at v10.26.0. `git cat-file -p 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887` provided the BIC-only authorship and trailer evidence.
reasoning: The vulnerability is reachable whenever untrusted data is rendered through the built-in strip_html filter: String.replace evaluates the lazy regex synchronously, so repeated unmatched openers force suffix rescans and block the event loop. The 2018 commit is the smallest real BIC because it directly replaced a non-equivalent, locally bounded tag matcher with the vulnerable lazy-alternative construction; its immediate parent tree has none of those alternatives. The 2019 TypeScript relocation, 2022 rename, 2023 multiline [\s\S] expansion, 2024 memory accounting, and 2026 generic-tag multiline expansion are not BICs because history shows the same repeated-unmatched-opener mechanism already existed. The release boundary corroborates causality: the BIC first appears in v3.1.3, the vulnerable form remains in v10.25.7, and the advisory fix first appears in v10.26.0. Fix commit 3616a744b9abeb425c217b340a2397d46176afb8 removes the regex and implements a terminating single-pass scanner. Finally, the BIC's own commit object has only human identities and no AI marker; later history cannot attribute this 2018 introduction to AI, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
